text:
jess: Heads-up — after flipping on TE FP8 for L40S we saw a clear latency spike and intermittent NaNs in the attention path. Repro when batch_size >= 8 and seq_len >= 1024. H100 runs look okay. Anyone bumped into this?

mike: Can you paste the exact error/log and the transformer engine config you used? :eyes:

jess: Paste from the run: 
```
E 03:12:21 attention.cpp:512 - INF value detected in softmax (NaN)
W 03:12:21 te_kernel_fallback - kernel fallback triggered: FP8->fallback(INT8)
I 03:12:21 runtime - fallback path latency +52ms
```
Config: `transformer_engine_precision = fp8`, `calibration_mode = per-tensor`, `te_kernel_hint = auto`

anita: I saw something similar on L40S last sprint. My suspicion: calibration stats collected on short seqs bias the FP8 scale when actual seq_len is long — leads to overflow/underflow in attention matmul. L40S's math lower-level kernels also react differently than H100.

raj: Also worth checking KV cache pressure. Our batcher bumps combined KV memory usage up quickly for batch>=8; TE internal scratch + KV reserve causes memory fragmentation -> occasional OOM then fallback. We have a heuristic that flushes older KV when mem>80%. That could interact badly with FP8 accumulator ranges.

mike: Ran microprofile on a repro workload, comparison below (avg over 100 iters):
```
kernel_name                      time_us   calls
matmul_kernel_FP8_v2             92.4     120
matmul_kernel_INT8               68.7     120
attention_softmax_fp8            15.1     120
attention_softmax_fallback      67.8     8
```
On H100 the FP8 kernel was ~20% faster than INT8. On L40S FP8 is slower — cost likely from extra scaling + branching when calibration parameters are borderline.

perf-bot: regression-alert: fp8-l40s-branch increased p95_token_latency by 48% vs baseline (2026-03-14). Linked run: https://perf.internal/runs/7891 :warning:

jess: I tried forcing TE to use INT8 on L40S (`te_kernel_hint = int8`) — latency normalized but ppl rose by ~0.28 on eval set. So quality hit but stable runtime.

anita: Two immediate mitigations: 1) improve calibration dataset to include long sequences and worst-case tokens; 2) add a per-device kernel selection override: prefer INT8 on L40S when seq_len >= 1024 or batch >= 8.

raj: I'll open an infra ticket to add a KV reservation knob per-device so we can keep a 20% reserve for TE scratch on L40S. That should reduce eviction-induced fallbacks. Ticket: #789 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENGINF-789)

mike: For longer term — we should add a runtime probe at start-of-epoch that runs a small matmul calibration to surface unstable FP8 ranges and mark device as `fp8_unsafe` if results diverge from fp32 beyond threshold. Then kernel_selector can prefer safe kernels automatically.

jess: +1. For now I'll: set `max_batch_for_fp8 = 4` on L40S in config, enable per-channel calibration with 1k warmup tokens, and re-run the nightly perf job.

perf-bot: scheduled job: nightly-fp8-l40s-repro (run_id=1829012399) queued :white_check_mark:

anita: If repro persists after per-channel cal, we may need TE kernel bug triage with vendor. Keep logs and the small repro binary handy.

mike: I'll push a branch with conservative batcher heuristics + device-level kernel hints. Assigning to eng-ml for validation.

jess: Thanks — posting perf dumps and a tiny repro in the ticket. Will follow up when nightly completes. :thumbsup:
